draft.title: Scatterplots
card: A scatterplot shows pairs of numerical data as points on a graph. Each point is one person, place, object or time, with a value for each of two variables.
the variable that may explain or influence the other. It goes on the x-axis (horizontal). Choose it by asking which may explain the other, not by number size or the order measured.
the variable that may respond to the change. It goes on the y-axis (vertical).

Example: Sam records hours of study and test mark for 12 students. Hours may explain the mark, so hours go on the x-axis and mark on the y-axis. A student with 3 hours and a mark of 60 is plotted at (3, 60).
draft.remember: Plot each pair as a point, with the explanatory variable on the x-axis.

a.q: A teacher compares each student's hours of sleep the night before with their number of mistakes on a maths quiz. Which variable is placed on the horizontal axis of the scatterplot?
opts: Hours of sleep, as it may explain the mistakes
Mistakes, as it may explain the hours of sleep
Mistakes, as it is the larger number
Hours of sleep, as it is measured first
a.why: Sleep may influence how many mistakes are made, so it is the explanatory variable and goes on the x-axis. The size of the numbers or the order of measuring does not decide the axis.
a.clue: Which variable may explain the other?

b.q: Mia records the daily maximum temperature and the number of ice creams sold at her stall in Lorne, Victoria. She draws a scatterplot to see if the two are related. On Monday it was 30°C and she sold 85. Which point is plotted for Monday?
b.why: Temperature may explain sales, so it is the explanatory variable and goes on the x-axis. Monday is plotted as (30, 85). The point (85, 30) swaps the axes.
b.clue: Which variable might explain the other? It is the x value.

a.best: Hours of sleep, as it may explain the mistakes
